findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted condition and wrong substring offsets, so it never checks the grant type
findings.body: The token id format is `<st:2><tt:2><gt:2>:<uuid>`, so the grant shortcut is at indices 4..6, i.e. `substring(4, 6)`. The matcher uses `substring(3, 5)`, which returns the last char of the token type plus the first char of the grant (e.g. "ta" for "onrtac"). The condition is also inverted: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects a match instead of a mismatch. The two bugs together mean the grant shortcut is never verified, and the check can only fail by accident (e.g. if the shifted substring happens to equal the shortcut). Every event assertion built on it (`expectCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken`, `expectAuthReqIdToToken`) only checks the `xxx:uuid` shape, not the encoded grant. It should be `!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)`, and the length of `items[0]` should be checked first. The comment saying "4th char" is also misleading.

findings.title: Null check for rawTokenId actually checks grantType
findings.body: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` re-checks `grantType` (already checked on the line above) instead of `rawTokenId`. A null `rawTokenId` is therefore accepted and the constructor builds a context with a null raw id. `encodeTokenId` would then produce an id ending in the string "null" (e.g. `onrtac:null`).

findings.title: testIncorrectGrantType passes because of an NPE, not the intended validation
findings.body: In `before()` only `factory.init(null)` is called, so `sessionFactory` stays null. For the unknown shortcut "ac", `getGrantTypeByShortcut` misses in the map and falls into the fallback path `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)`, which throws a NullPointerException. The test's `catch (RuntimeException iae)` swallows it, so the test passes without ever reaching the `IllegalArgumentException("Unknown value ... for grant type")` branch. The catch should be narrowed to `IllegalArgumentException`, and the factory given a mock or real session factory. There is also no test for `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` (session-type detection, default "na" grant), nor for malformed ids such as a wrong context length or unknown session type.

findings.title: Grant shortcut length is not validated, and the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory javadoc says '3-letters'
findings.body: The decoder requires the encoded context to be exactly 6 chars and slices the grant shortcut as chars 4..6, so every shortcut must be exactly 2 characters. `postInit` only checks for duplicates and never validates length or null. A custom or future grant factory returning e.g. a 3-letter shortcut (which the new javadoc on `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut` says is the usual form: "usually like 3-letters shortcut") produces ids such as `onrtabc:uuid`. These ids cannot be decoded ("Expected length of 6" error). A null shortcut makes `ConcurrentHashMap.put` throw an NPE and fail startup with an unhelpful error. Validate `shortcut != null && shortcut.length() == 2` in `postInit` (and in the lazy-refresh paths) and fix the javadoc to state the 2-character requirement.

findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
findings.body: `getShortcut()` is added as an abstract method with no default. Any third-party `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` fails to compile, or fails at startup with `AbstractMethodError` from `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit`. That takes down the whole server rather than just the new feature. A default implementation (or a graceful fallback in the encoder for factories without a shortcut) would avoid the break.

findings.title: Access token issued together with a new offline session is tagged as ONLINE
findings.body: The session type is derived from `userSession.isOffline()` at access-token creation time. For a code or password flow with the `offline_access` scope, `createTokenResponse` / the ROPC grant creates the access token from the online user session first. The offline session is only created later, in `generateRefreshToken`, and the online session may then be removed (`FIRST_OFFLINE_ACCESS` / direct grant). The access token id therefore says `on...`, while only the offline session exists afterwards. The stated purpose is to let later endpoints look up only the correct session type, so such tokens would send consumers to a session that no longer exists. The offline-ness should be derived from the requested scope / refresh token type, not only from the session used at issue time.

findings.title: Client credentials grant never sets the GRANT_TYPE attribute, so its tokens get 'na'
findings.body: Grant type is recorded explicitly in `createTokenResponse` (used by the auth-code, device and CIBA grants), in ROPC, pre-authorized code, refresh and standard token exchange. The client credentials grant is not touched by this PR, and neither are the UMA/permission grant or the legacy (V1) token exchange paths. Their access tokens are therefore always encoded with the `na` grant, although the factories were given shortcuts (`cc`, `pg`, ...) and the unit test treats `trltcc:` ids as normal. The grant-type information promised by the PR is silently missing for these flows.

findings.title: Access token jti format change (non-UUID) is user-visible but undocumented
findings.body: Access token `jti` was previously a plain UUID and is now `<6 chars>:<uuid>` (e.g. `onrtac:1f65...`). Clients, resource servers, log pipelines or custom providers that assume `jti` is a UUID will break, and this is not mentioned in the upgrading or release notes. Token id parsing (`getTokenContextFromTokenId`) also throws `IllegalArgumentException` for any id containing `:` that does not match the 6-char format, so callers must handle that.
